topics.title: Relevant Definitions for Input Tax Credit
explain: Input means any goods other than capital goods used or intended to be used in business.
Input service means any service used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business.
Capital goods are goods whose value is capitalised in the books of account of the person claiming ITC and used for business.
Exempt supply includes nil-rated supplies, wholly exempt supplies under Section 11 / IGST Section 6, and non-taxable supplies.
Input tax includes CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST charged on inward supplies, IGST on imports, and tax paid under reverse charge, but excludes composition tax.

flow.title: Classification of Inward Supply and Credit Eligibility
steps: Procure Goods or Services
Check Capitalisation in Books
Classify as Input Input Service or Capital Goods
Verify Tax Component Charged
Confirm Usage for Business Purpose
Avail Credit in Electronic Credit Ledger

topics.example: A shoe manufacturer purchasing leather gets 'Inputs', paying for electricity gets 'Input Services', and buying a cutting machine capitalised in books gets 'Capital Goods'.
remember: Composition levy tax paid on inward supplies is never eligible as Input Tax Credit.
Capital goods must be capitalised in the recipient's books of account.
mistakes: Treating capitalised machinery as regular inputs rather than capital goods.

quiz.q: Which of the following is excluded from the definition of Input Tax under Section 2(62)?
o: IGST charged on import of goods
Tax payable under reverse charge mechanism
CGST charged on inward supply of raw materials
quiz.why: Section 2(62) explicitly excludes tax paid under the composition levy from the definition of input tax.

quiz.q: What is the key requirement for goods to be classified as 'Capital Goods' under Section 2(19)?
o: They must be used within 30 days
Their value must be capitalised in books of account
They must be imported from outside India
They must be sold without further processing
quiz.why: Capital goods means goods whose value is capitalised in the books of account of the person claiming ITC.

topics.title: Eligibility and Conditions for Claiming ITC
explain: Every registered person can claim ITC on inward supplies used or intended for business use.

Six conditions must be met: possession of tax document, details uploaded by supplier in GSTR-1/IFF and visible in recipient's GSTR-2B, actual receipt of goods/services, credit not restricted u/s 38, tax paid by supplier to Government, and return filed u/s 39.
Bill-to-Ship-to model deems goods/services as received when delivered to a third party on the order of the registered buyer.
If goods are received in lots or instalments, ITC can only be claimed upon receipt of the last lot.
Recipient must pay the supplier value plus tax within 180 days from invoice date; failure requires reversal of ITC with interest (re-availment allowed on payment).
Time limit to claim ITC is 30th November following the end of financial year or date of filing annual return, whichever is earlier.

flow.title: Steps for Claiming and Retaining ITC
steps: Possess Valid Tax Document
Verify Details in Form GSTR-2B
Receive Goods or Services or Final Lot
File Form GSTR-3B Return
Pay Supplier Value plus Tax in 180 Days

topics.example: A company buys 10 MT of raw material to be delivered in three instalments from August to October. The company can claim ITC only in October when the final lot is received.
remember: Time limit u/s 16(4) is 30th November of next FY or annual return filing date, whichever is earlier.
Reversal due to non-payment within 180 days requires interest, but re-availment has no time limit once payment is made.
mistakes: Claiming proportionate ITC on receipt of the first lot when goods are delivered in instalments.

quiz.q: By when must a registered buyer pay the supplier to avoid reversing the availed ITC?
quiz.why: Second proviso to Section 16(2) mandates payment within 180 days from the date of issue of invoice.

quiz.q: What is the time limit for claiming ITC on an invoice pertaining to FY 2024-25 if the annual return is filed on 10th November 2025?
quiz.why: The time limit is 30th November following FY end or date of filing annual return, whichever is earlier.

topics.title: Apportionment of Credit & Blocked Credits
explain: ITC is restricted proportionately to business use and for making taxable or zero-rated supplies. No ITC for non-business or exempt supplies.
Section 17(5) blocks ITC on motor vehicles for passenger transport (seating capacity up to 13) unless used for further supply, passenger transport, or driving training.
ITC is blocked on general insurance, servicing, and repairs of ineligible motor vehicles, vessels, and aircrafts.
ITC is blocked on food, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, club membership, travel benefits, unless used for sub-contracting or mandatory under law for employees.
ITC is blocked on works contract and self-construction of immovable property (capitalised), except for plant and machinery.
ITC is blocked on goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off, given as gifts/free samples, CSR purchases, composition supplies, and tax paid under fraud cases.

flow.title: Filtering Inward Supplies for Credit Eligibility
steps: Identify Inward Supply
Check Blocked Credit List u/s 17(5)
If Blocked Disallow Full ITC
If Eligible Check Usage Purpose
Apportion for Business vs Non-Business
Apportion for Taxable vs Exempt Supplies
Claim Net Eligible Credit

topics.example: A manufacturing firm buying a car for executive travel cannot claim ITC, but an auto dealer buying demo cars for trial runs can claim ITC as it is for further supply.
remember: Plant and machinery excludes land, building, civil structures, telecom towers, and external pipelines.
Demo vehicles used by car dealers qualify for ITC as they promote further supply.
mistakes: Claiming ITC on goods lost, stolen, destroyed, or given away as free samples.

quiz.q: Under Section 17(5), ITC on motor vehicles with seating capacity up to 13 persons is ALLOWED when used for:
o: Imparting training on driving such motor vehicles
Free delivery of gifts to customers
quiz.why: Driving training is one of the statutory exceptions allowing ITC on passenger motor vehicles with seating <= 13.

quiz.q: Is ITC available on goods purchased for fulfilling Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) obligations?
o: Allowed up to 50% of tax paid
quiz.why: Section 17(5)(fa) explicitly blocks ITC on goods or services used for CSR obligations under Companies Act.

topics.title: Availability of Credit in Special Circumstances
explain: New registrants applying within 30 days can claim ITC on inputs in stock/WIP/finished goods on the day before liability date (No capital goods ITC).
Voluntary registration allows ITC on inputs held in stock/WIP/finished goods on the day before grant of registration (No capital goods ITC).
Switching from Composition to Regular or Exempt becoming Taxable allows ITC on inputs in stock and capital goods (reduced by 5% per quarter/part thereof).
Switching to Composition or Taxable becoming Exempt requires reversal of ITC on inputs in stock and capital goods on pro-rata basis (useful life taken as 5 years / 60 months).
Sale of capital goods on which ITC was taken requires payment of higher of: ITC reduced by 5% per quarter OR tax on transaction value.
Business reorganisation (merger, demerger, sale) allows transfer of unutilised ITC to the new entity via FORM GST ITC-02.

flow.title: Processing Credit under Special Circumstances
steps: Identify Trigger Event
Determine Stock and Assets on Cutoff Date
Calculate Input and Capital Goods Credit
Apply 5 Percent Per Quarter Reduction if Applicable
File Declaration in Form GST ITC-01 or ITC-03
Verify Supplier Details on Common Portal

topics.example: A dealer exiting composition scheme on 1st July can claim ITC on inputs in stock and capital goods held on 30th June, reducing capital goods ITC by 5% per quarter from invoice date.
remember: Useful life of capital goods is fixed at 5 years (60 months) for pro-rata credit reversal under Rule 44.
New registrants and voluntary registrants get ITC on inputs ONLY, not on capital goods.
mistakes: Claiming ITC on capital goods when taking voluntary registration.

quiz.q: A person taking voluntary registration can claim ITC on which of the following items held on the day preceding registration?
o: Inputs in stock and capital goods
Inputs held in stock, WIP, and finished goods
quiz.why: Section 18(1)(b) allows voluntary registrants ITC on inputs in stock/WIP/finished goods, but NOT on capital goods.

quiz.q: What is the assumed useful life of capital goods for calculating ITC reversal under Rule 44?
quiz.why: Rule 44 prescribes useful life of capital goods as 5 years (60 months) on pro-rata basis.

topics.title: Manner of Utilisation of ITC and Restrictions
explain: ITC of IGST must be completely exhausted first towards IGST liability, and then towards CGST and SGST/UTGST in any order and proportion.
ITC of CGST is used for CGST first, then IGST. It CANNOT be used to pay SGST/UTGST.
ITC of SGST/UTGST is used for SGST/UTGST first, then IGST (only after CGST credit is fully exhausted for IGST). It CANNOT be used to pay CGST.
Rule 86A empowers officers to block Electronic Credit Ledger if ITC is fraudulently availed or ineligible.
Rule 86B restricts credit ledger utilisation to 99% of output tax liability if monthly taxable turnover exceeds Rs 50 Lakhs (at least 1% must be paid in cash).
Exceptions to Rule 86B include taxpayers who paid > Rs 1 Lakh income tax in last 2 FYs, received > Rs 1 Lakh refund on exports/inverted duty, or Govt/PSUs.

flow.title: Order of Utilisation of Input Tax Credit
steps: Determine Output Liabilities for IGST CGST SGST
Fully Exhaust IGST Credit against IGST then CGST SGST
Utilise CGST Credit against CGST then IGST
Utilise SGST Credit against SGST then IGST
Apply Rule 86B Min 1 Percent Cash Rule if Applicable
Pay Balance Output Liability via Cash Ledger

topics.example: If output IGST is Rs 1,000 and IGST credit is Rs 1,300, Rs 1,000 pays IGST and the remaining Rs 300 can be used to pay output CGST or SGST in any proportion.
remember: Cross-utilisation between CGST and SGST/UTGST is strictly prohibited under GST law.
Entire IGST ITC balance must be NIL before using CGST or SGST credit for IGST.
mistakes: Utilising CGST credit balance to discharge SGST output tax liability.

quiz.q: Which Input Tax Credit balance must be completely exhausted before CGST or SGST credit can be utilised?
quiz.why: Section 49A and Rule 88A mandate that IGST credit must be fully exhausted before using CGST or SGST credit.

quiz.q: Under Rule 86B, what minimum percentage of output tax liability must be paid in cash if monthly taxable supplies exceed Rs 50 Lakhs?
quiz.why: Rule 86B restricts credit ledger use to 99% of output tax liability, forcing a minimum of 1% to be paid via cash ledger.
